rationale: The hypothesis is directly corroborated by the comprehensive primary multi-cohort study by Leitão et al. (2026) analyzing 34,329 individuals with rare disorders. In that study, exactly 141 individuals with RNU2-2 variants were identified, including 35 carrying recurrent dominant pathogenic variants and 91 affected individuals across 73 families harboring biallelic recessive variants. Parallel genomic studies by Jackson et al. (2026) and Greene et al. (2026) independently confirm that biallelic recessive RNU2-2 mutations represent an extraordinarily prevalent etiology of recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathy / neurodevelopmental disorder, establishing that the recessive form exceeds the dominant form in prevalence.

evidence.text: Leitão et al. identified RNU2-2 variants in 141 individuals, comprising 35 individuals with recurrent dominant variants and 91 affected members from 73 families with biallelic variants, documenting that recessive RNU2-2 neurodevelopmental disorder is at least twice as frequent as the dominant form.

source.title: Systematic analysis of snRNA genes reveals frequent RNU2-2 variants in dominant and recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
source.quote: We report RNU2-2 variants in 141 individuals, including 35 with recurrent dominant pathogenic variants and 91 affected members from 73 families with biallelic variants. Recessive RNU2-2 NDD is at least twice as frequent as the dominant form

evidence.text: Clinical collation demonstrates that in the Leitão et al. discovery cohort, epilepsy occurred in 88% of dominant cases (28/32) and 83% of recessive cases (60/72), meeting criteria for developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.

source.title: Guide for Clinicians and Researchers | ReNU2 Foundation
source.quote: In Leitão et al., epilepsy occurred in 88% of dominant (28 of 32) and 83% of recessive (60 of 72) participants, and "patients with epilepsy met the criteria for developmental and epileptic encephalopathy."

evidence.text: Jackson et al. independently show that rare biallelic variants in RNU2-2 are significantly enriched and over-transmitted in neurodevelopmental disorders, causing a severe recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathy that is genetically and clinically distinct from the dominant RNU2-2 syndrome and by far the most frequent recessive NDD in their cohort.

source.title: Biallelic variants in RNU2-2 cause a remarkably frequent developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source.quote: We define a recessive RNU2-2 syndrome, delineate its unique genetic architecture and show that it manifests clinically as a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy... Within our cohort, the recessive RNU2-2 syndrome emerges as by far the most frequent recessive NDD

evidence.text: Greene et al. demonstrated that biallelic variants in RNU2-2 cause the most prevalent known recessive NDD, identifying 18 probands plus 5 affected siblings with high confidence and additional replication cases, accounting for approximately 10% of diagnosable recessive NDD families.

evidence.text: Krygier et al. assessed 76 dominant and recessive RNU2-2 cases and observed movement disorders in 29 of 76 patients (38%), noting they presented more frequently in biallelic recessive individuals.

new_directions.question_text: What specific neurological signs (e.g. movement disorder sub-phenotypes or seizure semiology) reliably distinguish dominant de novo RNU2-2 encephalopathy from biallelic recessive RNU2-2 encephalopathy?
new_directions.rationale: While both modes of inheritance share severe developmental delay and high epilepsy rates (>80%), Krygier et al. noted hyperkinetic movement disorders are significantly enriched in biallelic cases, warranting systematic head-to-head clinical phenotyping.

new_directions.question_text: Can the ratio of U2-2 to its paralog U2-1 serve as a sensitive clinical biomarker to discriminate between monoallelic dominant and biallelic recessive RNU2-2 cases?
new_directions.rationale: Jackson et al. and Greene et al. observed marked reduction (>90%) of pathogenic U2-2 transcripts in biallelic individuals with wild-type compensation in monoallelic carriers, suggesting transcript dosage ratios could offer diagnostic resolution.
